tenet: Make functions total — widen the output so the caller must handle the missing case
why_discriminating: The naive solution reaches for the panicking (`items[index]!`) or defaulting (`items.getD index 0`) accessor to return a bare Int — both compile. The skillful solution widens the return to Option Int (`items[index]?`), so `get [1, 2, 3] 99 + 1` fails elaboration. (Lean also offers a third, better-than-Option design — requiring a bounds proof — but the neutral prompt gives no proof to pass, so Option is the natural safe design here.) The prompt is NEUTRAL: it never mentions the out-of-bounds case.
prompt: Write Lean 4 code exposing a public function `get (items : List Int) (index : Nat)` that returns the element at `index` in `items`. Output only top-level declarations — no `main`, no `#check`/`#eval` demos.
